title: Adaptive request shaping and priority eviction for regional dependency resilience
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Owner: ENG infra. Problem: downstream stores (Redis user cache, Kafka event store, primary DB) occasionally cross degradation thresholds during regional spikes or partial outages. Current mitigation (global circuit breakers + blunt shedding) causes tenant unfairness and noisy failovers across regions. This ticket designs and implements an adaptive shaping + priority eviction layer in the connection/adapter layer to provide per-tenant fairness, bounded tail latency, and predictable SLO behavior while enabling fast cross-region fallback to read-only degraded modes.
background: We have repeated production incidents where a regional network blip or a noisy tenant causes connection pool exhaustion against Redis or DB replicas, sending load to fallback regions and cascading increased latency. Existing global shedding is binary and tends to over-shed low-priority traffic instead of protecting high-priority flows. Engineering needs a hybrid approach: shape ingress to dependencies with per-tenant quotas, prioritized admission lanes, and an eviction policy that prefers cacheable or non-critical work. This must integrate with multi-region routing and the rollout/console observability features.
goals: Limit P99 latency amplification on downstream stores under partial failure to <= 2x baseline
Maintain throughput for high-priority tenant lanes during regional degradation
Avoid full-service cascades when a single downstream saturates
Provide clear telemetry in Console for troubleshooting and post-incident analysis
non_goals: Replace existing global circuit-breaker architecture (this augments it)
Re-architect Kafka consumer groups — only adapter-level admission & backpressure
proposed_solution: Introduce an adapter layer component (shaper) sitting in front of each downstream client (Redis, Kafka producer, DB pool). The shaper implements: (1) hierarchical token-bucket for admission: global pool, region pool, per-tenant logical buckets; (2) lane-based priority queueing (critical | normal | best-effort) with size-limited fast-path; (3) priority-aware eviction for cache/write patterns: prefer dropping best-effort cache-priming writes and background indexing tasks; (4) soft-fallback mode where reads degrade to tombstone/TTL-extended cache reads and DB queries are routed to read-replicas with staleness metadata. The shaper emits metrics (admissions, rejections, waits, evictions) and events to Console and integrates with rollouts to allow canary of different thresholds. Admission thresholds are SLO-driven and auto-tunable via closed-loop feedback from observed token consumption and tail latency.
design_decisions: Use token-bucket over static quotas to allow short bursts while enforcing long-term fairness
Implement lane prioritization in-memory per adapter to avoid extra RTTs to central services
Eviction policy will be pluggable: default 'least-impact' heuristic (evict best-effort cache writes first), with optional tenant-weight overrides
Soft-fallback decisions made locally with config sync from control plane; no control-plane dependency in the fast path
Expose per-tenant admission metrics with tenant hashed ID (non-PII) to Console for cost and SLA attribution
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary - 2 weeks): deploy shaper to 1 region on read path only for low-risk tenants; monitor P95/P99 and admission rates
Phase B (limited write shaping): enable write-path shaping for canary tenants and observe application errors/retries; tune eviction heuristics
Phase C (regional ramp): extend to 3 regions with tiered thresholds; enable auto-tune feedback loop in shadow mode
Phase D (global): enable shaping by default with per-customer opt-outs and Console controls
Rollback: revert to shadow-only mode or disable adapter if error rates or customer impact exceed thresholds defined in acceptance criteria
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket logic, lane priority enforcement, and eviction heuristics
Integration tests simulating multi-tenant mixes and induced downstream latency to verify admissions and evictions
Chaos test: in staging, simulate partial region outage (network partition) and validate that shaping prevents pool exhaustion and keeps high-priority lanes healthy
Load test: bake with realistic tail distributions collected from production traces and validate P99 behavior under synthetic noisy-tenant patterns
Canary verification checklist and automated canary gates (latency, errors, rejected_admissions rate)
monitoring_and_alerting: New Console dashboards: admissions by lane, per-tenant rejection rate, eviction counts, average wait time, downstream round-trip per adapter
SLO alarms: P99 latency increase > 1.8x baseline for 5m triggers PagerDuty
Operational alerts: admission rejection spike (>0.5% global or >3% per-tenant for >10m), sustained eviction rate > threshold
Runbooks: steps to throttle low-priority lanes, adjust token refill rates, or force soft-fallback mode per region
acceptance_criteria: Under simulated partial region outage, admission shaping prevents connection pool exhaustion and keeps high-priority lanes operating (no more than 2% increase in error rate for high-priority requests)
P99 for downstream requests (Redis/DB) remains <= 2x baseline during stress tests
Console surfaces per-tenant admission metrics and eviction reasons; product/SE can produce report linking rejections to billing/SLAs
Canary rollout completed in three regions with configurable thresholds and no customer-facing incidents for 72h after full enablement
open_questions: How should tenant weights be bootstrapped for new customers? (proposal: default equal weight, allow weights via account API)
What is the acceptable eviction budget for batch/background jobs vs interactive traffic?
Should eviction records be retained in audit logs or sampled to control storage costs?
Do we need an operator-visible override in Console to instantly drain best-effort lanes for an incident?
dependencies: PM-4125 (pricing-affecting-tenant-weights) - product decision on tenant billing attribution
notes: Prototype implemented in Go in feature branch 'shaper/adapter-v1' — basic token-bucket + lane queueing done
Initial microbench shows additional median latency ~0.6ms and a 2% CPU increase at adapter layer; acceptable trade-off for tail protection
Will coordinate with infra team to instrument read-replica routing for soft-fallback
We should schedule a 1-hour design review with Product and Security to finalize tenant telemetry redaction rules
